assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour put to work: pH-dependent charge, hexagonal/inverted-phase propensity and controlled particle formation enable nucleic-acid encapsulation and endosomal release. The concept is original, physically explainable and has had very large clinical and societal impact (siRNA and mRNA medicines). From my soft-matter view it is a case where membrane physical chemistry decided the outcome.
assessment.attribution: The decisive lipid-formulation work (early LNP encapsulation, ionizable lipids, scalable mixing) is most clearly associated with the Vancouver group; Cullis led it, with Madden and Hope central to the encapsulation and formulation chemistry. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed to lipidoid and clinical translation but are left out to keep a three-person prize; the split between lipid-delivery and RNA-modification credit (already recognised in 2023 Medicine) needs care.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale (Onpattro, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines) and independently reproduced; the science is stable and recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize may make some members feel the area was already honoured.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry framing is distinct enough from the 2023 Medicine prize
Fair division of credit among the many Vancouver, MIT and industry contributors
My recollection of who invented specific ionizable lipids is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as liquid-liquid phase separation governed by multivalency, weak interactions and thermodynamic phase diagrams. This is a new concept of molecular organisation that physical chemists recognise at once, with wide influence across cell biology, disease and materials.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules, the founding observation; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction physical framework. Pappu and Mittag made major sequence-grammar contributions, so the three-person limit leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and still contested on in vivo relevance, definitions of condensates and how much is truly equilibrium phase separation; recognition is arguably somewhat early but the concept is broadly adopted.
uncertainties: Debate on whether many reported condensates are true phase-separated liquids in vivo
Exclusion of Pappu and Mittag from a three-person prize
Chemistry versus biology classification of the prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory resolved the Levinthal paradox and gave a thermodynamic and statistical-mechanical framework for folding, with wide extension to function and disordered proteins. It is a general physical-chemical principle, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic developed the funnel and minimal-frustration theory; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model work was complementary, and Fersht's experimental mapping is arguably the experimental counterpart. Bryngelson is a co-originator with Wolynes. The credit split between theory and experiment is the main issue.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely accepted and tested by experiment and simulation, though a large part of the community now gives AI structure prediction the headlines (2024 Chemistry); the theory remains foundational and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether to include Fersht or Bryngelson for fairness
Overlap with the 2024 prize may reduce appetite
Predictive versus conceptual character of the theory

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers delivered a very rapid rise in solar-cell efficiency from about 4 percent to over 25 percent, with defect-tolerant semiconductor chemistry of broad significance for energy and optoelectronics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in photovoltaic cells; Park's solid-state cells and Snaith's thin-film device and mixed-halide work were decisive. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also made major contributions; the credit is crowded and contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently reproduced worldwide, but long-term stability and commercial deployment are unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead toxicity at scale
Crowded attribution, including Grätzel and Seok
Whether application maturity matches the Nobel standard

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate nonstandard amino acids, a general method that changed protein engineering, chemical biology and the study of protein function.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and co-workers established the first orthogonal pairs in vivo and the general strategy; Chin extended it to multiple codons and eukaryotes and ribosome engineering; Wang was an early Schultz-lab contributor. Mehl and Yokoyama have meaningful roles, so credit is partly ambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and reproducible for over two decades, so mature and timely.
uncertainties: Division of credit among Schultz-lab alumni
Substantial adjacency to the 2018 and 2024 directed-evolution and protein prizes
Practical limits on yields and scope for multiple residues

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframed small-molecule pharmacology by inducing proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, with a physical-chemical logic of ternary-complex cooperativity and a pipeline now in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs; Ciulli provided structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex principles. Handa, Ito and others uncovered the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues, which is a distinct compound strand.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical data are encouraging but approved drugs from the PROTAC branch are not yet established, so recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Lack of approved PROTAC drugs
Separate treatment of molecular-glue credit
Possible Medicine-prize overlap

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase and so reveals stoichiometry, subunit connectivity and ligand binding, including membrane protein-lipid interactions that I find relevant to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the clearest leader for intact complexes and membrane proteins; Heck and Chait developed key methodology and applications. Loo and Gross have earlier contributions, leaving ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Methods are widely adopted and independently confirmed; the main residual issue is the overlap with the 2002 ESI prize and with proteomics MS.
uncertainties: Whether gas-phase structures faithfully reflect solution structures in every case
Overlap with the earlier mass spectrometry Nobel
Crowded credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation-dispersion methods allow solution structure and dynamics of large proteins to be probed, including invisible excited states, which gives a physical-chemistry link between motion and function.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay were central to the triple-resonance and isotope-labelling methods and the TROSY- and relaxation-based advances; Wagner and Palmer also contributed. Wüthrich was recognised in 2002, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed, though a prize could be seen as incremental after the 2002 NMR award.
uncertainties: Distinguishing from the 2002 Wüthrich prize
Choosing between structure and dynamics contributions
Possible bias toward the NIH group
